sentences.text: Microraptor is a small genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaurs known for having four wings.
The holotype of M. gui measured 77 cm in length, with a wingspan ranging from 88 to 94 cm and a weight between 0.5 and 1.4 kg.
This animal possessed long pennaceous feathers on its arms and hands measuring 10 to 20 cm and on its legs and feet measuring 11 to 15 cm.
Microraptor was one of the most abundant non-avian dinosaurs in its ecosystem, with over 300 fossil specimens found across museums.
It remains the most abundant non-avian dinosaur fossil type found in the Jiufotang Formation.
One specimen shows evidence of active primary sequential moulting, a rare fossil behavior similar to that of modern flying birds.
The genus Microraptor was first described by Xu and colleagues in the year 2000.
The initial specimen was a chimeric patchwork of different dinosaur species assembled from multiple specimens and smuggled to the USA.
Mark Norell and colleagues described an unnamed Microraptor specimen, BPM 1 3-13, in 2002.
In March 2012, Li and colleagues determined the plumage coloration of Microraptor using the new specimen BMNHC PH881, which also revealed several previously unknown features.
Researchers originally hypothesized that Microraptor was an arboreal glider because its hindwings would have hindered ground running.
Microraptor likely had awkward ground movement because its hindwing feathers extended over most of its foot.
Wind tunnel experiments suggest Microraptor was most efficient when gliding between low elevations by sustaining high lift at the expense of high drag.
In 2005, Sankar Chatterjee suggested Microraptor's forewings and hindwings were on different levels like a biplane, as an overlaid posture would be anatomically impossible.
Chatterjee determined Microraptor likely used a phugoid gliding style, swooping in a deep U-shaped curve between perches.
In 2003, paleontologist Xu Xing described a Microraptor specimen as a "four-winged dinosaur" and speculated it could glide using all four limbs.
Research by Xu and colleagues in 2003 suggested that early dromaeosaurs were likely small, lived in trees, and were capable of gliding.
Subsequent studies have suggested that Microraptor was also capable of active flight.
The mammal in Microraptor's gut had an estimated snout-to-vent length of 80 mm and a mass of 13–43 g.

In 2010, researchers announced that additional preparation of the type specimen of M. zhaoianus revealed preserved stomach contents consisting of mammal bones, including possible skull fragments, limb parts, vertebrae, and an entire foot.
A 2011 study by Jingmai O'Connor and coauthors described a Microraptor gui specimen containing bones of an arboreal enantiornithean bird, including a partial wing and feet.
Microraptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae.
Microraptor is the parent group of the subfamily Microraptorinae.
Due to its frequent use and proper description, Microraptor is considered a nomen protectum while Archaeoraptor is a nomen vanum.
Microraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian stage, between 125 and 120 million years ago.
Microraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous, between 125 and 113 million years ago, in the Aptian stage in what is now Asia.
All Microraptor species originate from the Jiufotang Formation of the early Cretaceous Aptian stage, approximately 120 million years ago.
It is debated whether Microraptor consists of three distinct species or represents variation within a single species, M. zhaoianus.
There is debate regarding whether Storrs L. Olson successfully met all formal requirements to establish Archaeoraptor liaoningensis as a valid taxon.
Studies indicate that features distinguishing Cryptovolans are not unique and appear in varying degrees across Microraptor specimens.
